decisions.what: Implemented parallax via native scroll listener + requestAnimationFrame instead of Framer Motion's useScroll/useTransform.
decisions.why: The project has no framer-motion dependency listed among available imports; a lightweight scroll+rAF implementation preserves the requested translateY(scroll * factor) behavior, respects will-change: transform, and honors prefers-reduced-motion and the mobile media-query reduction the spec called for.

decisions.what: Reduced parallax on mobile rather than disabling it outright.
decisions.why: Spec says 'disable/reduce parallax on small screens'; a 0.25x factor is used on mobile to keep decorative motion subtle without eliminating it entirely, while prefers-reduced-motion still fully disables it.

decisions.what: Team card flip built with pure CSS 3D transforms and React state, not a motion library.
decisions.why: Keeps zero new runtime dependencies while meeting the spec's perspective/transform-style/rotateY(180deg) requirements. Click and Enter/Space toggle flip; ARIA role='button' and aria-pressed reflect state.

decisions.what: Intersection Observer used directly for scroll-triggered fade-in with 100ms stagger.
decisions.why: Matches spec literally ('observe each card', '100ms increments') and avoids external animation libs. Falls back to visible=true when IntersectionObserver isn't available (SSR/older environments).

decisions.what: TEAM_MEMBERS uses '/images/team/*.png' paths that resolve against the public/images/team directory.
decisions.why: OptimizedImage feeds src through the configured next/image loader; keeping paths under /images/team lets designers drop 400x400 PNGs in without further code changes, matching the spec for the placeholder directory.

decisions.what: Did not create an accompanying README.md next to public/images/team/.gitkeep.
decisions.why: Spec 008 target file is only the .gitkeep; the prompt's global 'NO MARKDOWN FILES' rule forbids creating .md files, so the README described in the spec text was omitted in favor of the explicit no-markdown constraint.
